Petitioner has filed this petition U/sec.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, claiming the compensation amount of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest from the respondents.

2. Petitioner case is as Follows:
That on 05.07.2024 at about 3.40 pm, he was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg No.KA-07-S-9907, in Bengaluru Chinthamani road, near Hyundai Showroom,
Dhanush P vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185250432/
1 wherein the driver of the Lorry beg. Reg.No.KA-01-AP- 6916, drove it with high speed, rash and negligent manner and he suddenly and negligently took right turn of his vehicle without giving signal as a result petitioner dashed against the lorry.
In the said accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

He was shifted to RL Jalappa hospital, wherein he took first aid, later he was shifted to Gaurav Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient for the accidental injuries and he has spent Rs.2,00,000/- for his treatment.
3. Petitioner stated that he is 24 years of age and he is working at TATA Electronics and he was earning Rs.25,000/- per month,

Further he stated that the accident occurred due the negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle and the jurisdictional police have registered Cr.No.56/2024 against the driver of the offending vehicle.

Petitioner alleged that the Respondent no.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle and he insured his vehicle with respondent no.1 and accident caused due to the sole negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and as such both are liable to pay the compensation with interest and he prayer this tribunal to award the compensation amount by allowing the petition.
4. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, Respondent No.1 appeared through its counsel filed power and written statement.
Respondent No.2 has not chosen to contest the petition and he placed exparte.

Respondent No.1 admitted the issuance of insurance policy to the vehicle of respondent No.2 and contended that the accident occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner and he falsely implanted the vehicle belongs to Respondent No.2 to claim the compensation prays this tribunal to dismiss the petition.
5. Petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and examined the doctor as PW.2, produced and marked 16 documents which are at Ex.P.1 to 16 and they are fully cross examined.
6. Respondent no.1 has not chosen to lead the evidence and their evidence is taken as nil.
7. I have heard the arguments from the counsel appearing for the petitioner.
Counsel appearing for respondent No.1 is permitted to file the written arguments on merits.
I have perused the same along with entire records.

8. On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following :
ISSUES 1.Whether

the petitioner proves that on 05.07.2024 at about 3.40 pm, he was riding motorcycle bearing Reg No.KA-07-S-9907, in Bengaluru Chinthamani road, near Hyundai Showroom, wherein the driver of the Lorry beg.

Reg.No.KA-01- Dhanush P vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185250432/
2 AP-6916, drove it with high speed, rash and negligent manner and he negligently took right turn without giving signal as a result petitioner dashed against the lorry.

sentences.text: In the said accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries as alleged in the petition.?

2 Whether respondent no.1 proves that accident occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner,
and petitioner was not having valid DL, as on the date of the accident as contended in the written statement.?
3.Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?

if so, what is the quantum and from whom?
4.What order or award?
9.

After carefully going through the evidence placed on record and taking into consideration of facts and attending circumstances of the case, my findings to the above issues are as follows;
Issue no.1: In the affirmative Issue no.2: In the negative Issue no.3: In partly affirmative Issue no.4:
As per final order for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1 to 3 :- I have taken these issues together for common discussion so as to avoid the repetition of facts and reasoning.
PW.1 being the petitioner, he reiterated the petition averments in his examination-in-chief affidavit.

Petitioner has tender the police records, that is C/copy of FIR, complaint, mahazar, sketch, IMV report, wound certificate, Final report, discharge summary, notice and reply U/s 133 of IMV Act which are at Ex.P.1 to 10.
11.
On careful perusal of the aforesaid undisputed documents, one Sri. Pradeep.B.P S/o Puttaswamy gowda was the driver of the offending vehicle as on the date of the accident.
Mahazar, sketch, IMV report, final report establishes the involvement of the offending vehicle and the negligent act of the driver in the alleged accident.

Further ExP.9 is the reply notice given by respondent No.2 wherein he admit that Pradeep was the driver of his vehicle and he was having valid driving license and insurance policy of the said vehicle was valid as on the date of the accident.
12. In the cross-examination of PW-1, nothing worth has been elicited to disprove the allegation.
The alleged negligent act of the petitioner is not suggested to PW-1.
Respondent No.1 has failed to establish its contention that accident occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner and vehicle belongs to respondent No.2 is falsely implanted.
Admittedly petitioner has sustained grievous injuries to his left leg in the accident.
Counsel for the petitioner argued that wearing of helmet by the petitioner as no impact and consequence as he had sustained leg injury and admittedly the petitioner has not sustained head injury.

sentences.text: The final report which is at Ex.P7 is filed after investigation and it is the prima facie proof of the accident and the involvement of the offending vehicle and rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly the police records cannot be doubted and disbelieved as it has reached the finality.

14. Petitioner has tender the wound certificate, discharge summary as per Ex.P.6,10, the entry therein reveals that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries that is left leg hole pettella fracture and lacerated wound.
Tension band wiring is done to fix the left leg patalla.
Further petitioner has taken treatment for the accidental injuries as inpatient for two 2 days.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the compensation under the following heads.

15. Pecuniary damages (Medical expenses) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization,
Medicines, Transportation, Nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure:
16. Petitioner took treatment at Gaurav hospital.
Evidently nothing is elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disbelieve the fact that he has sustained the grievous injuries in the alleged accident and he took treatment for the same.
Inasmuch, discharge summary, wound certificate and the medical reports issued form the hospital has to be accepted.
Admittedly petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient for 2 days, he has tendered bill for Rs.82,918/- as per Ex.P.11.
Further for the attendant charges, transportation, nourishing food, he might have spend some more expenses.
Therefore I award Rs.10,000/-, in total petitioner is entitled for Rs.92,918/- under this head.
Loss of income during laid up period.
17. The petitioner has not substantiated his nature of work and income as alleged in the petition.
Accident took place on 05.07.2024 however as per notional income chart, the notional income for the year 2024 is Rs.16,500/-, and same is assessed and considered as his monthly income.
Considering the accidental injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, I am of view that fifteen days, he has lost his income.
Therefore I award Rs.8,250/- as compensation under this head.
Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
18. The petitioner has examined the Orthopedic surgeon Sri.B.N.Nagaraj as PW-2.

He deposed that,
petitioner has 13% of whole body disability as per Ex.P15.
I have perused the evidence of PW-2 wound certificate, discharge summary given by the hospital, X-ray etc.
Evidently petitioner has not examined the doctor who has treated him in the hospital.
Petitioner sustained grievous injuries that is left leg hole patella fracture and lacerated wound.
Tension band wiring is done to fix the left leg patella of the petitioner.
Further doctor has admitted that fracture is united and petitioner is having no swelling and infection and he has no further complication.
The oral testimony of PW-2 corroborates with Ex.P.15 and 16.
Admittedly petitioner has no functional disability.
The percentage of loss of earning capacity due to accidental injuries is different from the percentage of physical disability due to accidental injuries.

Considering the medical reports and oral testimony of doctor, the whole body disability of Dhanush P vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185250432/
4

sentences.text: the petitioner is assessed as 9%.
The notional monthly income of the petitioner is assessed as Rs.16,500/-, the age of petitioner as on the date of accident is 24 years as per the entry in Aadhar card and DL which are at ExP.13 & 14.
The multiplier applicable to this case is "18".

Therefore loss of income on account of permanent disability is calculated as follows; Rs.16,500/-(Monthly income) X 12 (Months) X 18 ( Multiplier)
X9% (Disability) = Rs.3,20,760/- Hence, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.3,20,760/- as compensation under this head.
Non-Pecuniary damages (General damages) (IV)Damages for pain and sufferings and loss of amenities:
19.
It is undisputed fact that petitioner has sustained grievous injury.
During the hospitalization and rehabilitation period, he might have undergone lot of pain and sufferings and due to accidental injuries.
Therefore I award Rs.20,000/- under these conventional heads.

V) Loss of Amenities :-
20.
The petitioner has to forego certain amenities available for him.

Therefore I award Rs.20,000/-
as compensation under this head.
As per the oral testimony of PW-2, another surgery is required for the petitioner, for the removal of implants.
The estimated cost of the surgery is not tendered.
Tentatively petitioner is entitled for Rs.25,000/- for the additional surgery.
21. Except these heads the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under any other heads.
In all the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:
Sl No Particulars Amount

1 Towards medicines, attendant charges, Rs. 92,918/-
 transportation, nourishing food  2 Loss of income during the laid up period Rs. 8,250/-

3 Loss of income on account of Rs.3,20,760/-
 permanent disability  4 pain & sufferings Rs. 20,000/-
 5 loss of amenities Rs. 20,000/-
 6 Cost of additional surgery Rs. 25,000/-
. Rate of Interest:
The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s
Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
Accordingly I award the interest at the rate of 6% P.A on the compensation amount form the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
23. Liability:

The insurance company has not disputed the validity of the policy of the offending Dhanush P vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185250432/
5 vehicle, on the other hand, they have failed to established its defence that accident occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner.

Hence with the aforesaid discussion based on the evidence placed on record, Accordingly I am answering Issue No.1 the affirmative, issue No.2 in the negative and issue no.3 in partly affirmative.
24. Issue No.4:

For the foregoing reason and discussion, on point No.1, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor vehicle Act,1988, is partly allowed with cost.
Petitioner is entitled for the compensation amount of Rs.4,86,928/-with interest at the rate of 6% P.A from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
Respondent no.1 is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this tribunal with in 30 days from the date of the judgment.

After depositing the compensation amount with interest, Cash sheristedar is directed to release the entire amount to the petitioner through K2, after compliance of mandate of circular No.39/2020 dated 17.01.2020.
Advocate fee of Rs.1000/- is fixed.
All the interim applications pending if any stands disposed of.
Draw award accordingly.
